To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spermine synthase-deficient mice have no detectable spermine synthase enzyme activity and no spermine content, but have a higher spermidines content in all tissues examined.
Gy male mice and embryonic cells derived from them provide a model to study the importance and effects of spermine and the lack of spermidine synthase.
spermine-deficient mutant Gy male mice and spermine synthetase-deficient embryonic fibroblast cultures provide valuable models to investigate the importance of spermines in the cell and the organism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthesis and metabolism of the polyamines spermidine and spermine.
the role that polyamines play in normal and pathological conditions.
the biosynthesis and functions of the naturally occurring polyamines, which are ubiquitous polycationic molecules that are essential for normal cell growth and development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lack of spermidine/spermine N1-acetyl transferase activity in the spermine synthase knockout mice does not affect the growth or survival of embryonic fibroblast cultures, but does affect sensitivity to the chloroethylated nitrosourea.
spermine is not an essential polyamine in mammals.

the lack of spermin synthase activity in the Gy male mouse and in the fibroblasts derived from it does not have any significant effect on the development of the animal or on the growth or senescence of fibroblastic cell lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spermine is not required for the growth of fibroblastic cells in culture, and that spermine synthase is not an absolute essential gene for the survival and development of the mouse.
spermine is not an essential polyamine in mice, although it may have a role in the resistance of fibroblastic cells to killing by chloroethylating agents.
spermine is not essential for growth or for senescence, although it does provide protection from the effects of chloroethylating agents such as 1, 2-bis(2-hydroxyethyl)-N-ni-trosourea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absence of spermine synthases does not affect cell growth or senescence, but does increase the sensitivity of cells to the chloroethylamine 1,3-Bis(2-chlorethyl)-N-Nitrosourea.
spermine is not essential for cell growth or for the time of senesce of primary cultures of fibroblastic cells.
spermine synthase is important for the survival of embryonic fibroblast cultures in vitro, but not for the growth of fibroblastic cell lines in vitro or the growth of mice in vivo.
